authorship: AI review, authored by the DIS-RPLICE campaign loop (sprint 92, ledger item Q04). Not qualified human scientific acceptance, not clinical acceptance, and no patient benefit is claimed or implied.
change_from_0_1: period becomes a first-class field on every site object, so a per-site window cannot hide inside a single record-level string (S88-C4)

every one of the required dimensions must carry an explicit state and a reason on every record; absence is a validation failure, not a default (sprint 92 finding that 18 of 19 dimensions were absent yet the v0.1 validator returned PASS)
late_stage_share_percent must declare its construct, because the case proportion and the age-weighted rate ratio W coexist in the same record and differ by 0.7397 pp at Hinds and -0.5053 pp at Harris
claim_level is capped by comparison_status, so a CONDITIONAL comparison cannot carry a causal_candidate claim
follow_up_completion_after_abnormal_test is added as a required dimension, because the pilot's primary outcome was absent from v0.1 and neither system publishes it

records.reason: Both county figures are read from one rendered State Cancer Profiles table under one footnote set, so steward, case definition and denominator convention are shared at documentation level. The pair still cannot carry more than a descriptive claim because the stage variable actually used per county is undisclosed, the age-group count is stated two contradictory ways on the same page, and the pilot's primary outcome is unpublished for both counties.

denominator.why: Dagger footnote: population counts for denominators are based on Census populations as modified by NCI, with the US Population Data File used for SEER and NPCR incidence rates. The age-group count inside the age adjustment is separately UNKNOWN.
denominator.value: Census populations as modified by NCI, US Population Data File

age_adjustment.why: The same page states two incompatible age-group counts. Dagger footnote: 'SEER areas use 20 age groups and NPCR areas use 19 age groups'. CI*Rank footnote: 'The rates used in CI*Rank are all age-adjusted to the 2000 US standard population using 19 age groups for SEER and NPCR areas'. Both county rows show CI*Rank N/A, so the CI*Rank note does not govern the displayed rates. Neither statement can be preferred on this page.

case_definition.why: Dagger footnote: rates are for invasive cancer only except bladder, computed from cancers classified as malignant on ICD-O-3, with cancer=020 the colorectal site set.

stage_definition.why: The ^ footnote fixes late as regional or distant and names Combined Summary Stage with Expanded Regional Codes (2004+) for SEER and Merged Summary Stage for NPCR, but then reserves substitution: 'Due to the increased complexity with staging, other staging variables maybe used if necessary.' The variable actually used is not disclosed per county.

period.why: Report header states 2019-2023 for both county rows.

subgroup_coding.why: Table parameters fix the strata: race=00 All Races, sex=0 Both Sexes, age=001 All Ages.

suppression.why: Page states counts are suppressed below 16 records per area-sex-race category; the two county totals shown are far above that floor, but any age-stratified tabulation for Hinds does not clear it.

uncertainty.why: 95 percent confidence intervals printed beside each rate.

publication_latency.why: The page states a creation timestamp but not the registry data vintage or the release-to-publication interval for this window.

decision_owner.why: No named owner, reviewer or adjudicator is attached to this comparison in either repository or in the pilot register.

actionability.why: No action, threshold or owner is bound to this comparison; the sprint 78 counterfactual remains a proposal without an adopting body.

follow_up_completion_after_abnormal_test.why: Neither system publishes this quantity at county level, and the pilot's primary outcome has never been measured. When valued it must be: numerator, individuals with an abnormal screening-indication colorectal test who had a completed diagnostic colonoscopy with pathology documented within 180 days of the abnormal result; denominator, individuals with an abnormal screening-indication colorectal test in the same window; exclusions named in advance. A test ordered does not populate the numerator.
